themes_detail.label: Standing Water Surge
themes_detail.summary: Standing water complaints spiked to 4 reports THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1500% increase (z-score: 8.66)—signaling potential drainage failures, flooding risk, or sewage backups that demand immediate infrastructure investigation.
evidence: 4 standing water complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike)
Z-score of 8.66 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Timing coincides with recent weather patterns—potential drainage system failure in specific neighborhoods
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to identify which streets/storm drains are failing and whether flooding poses risk to residents or basements
Interview affected residents about water pooling locations and whether sewage backup is involved

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 103 reports LAST WEEK versus a 24.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 323% spike (z-score: 5.59)—suggesting construction, special events, or enforcement gaps warrant urgent scrutiny.
evidence: 103 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 24.4 weekly baseline (323% increase)
Z-score of 5.59 indicates highly significant statistical anomaly
Concurrent spike in commercial noise (14 complaints last week vs. 5.1 avg, 173% increase)
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify if construction permits (DOB filed 625 permits in 90 days, 430 alterations) correlate with noise spike
Interview 311 callers about sources: late-night construction, bars/venues, or vehicle violations (illegal parking enforcement absent?)

themes_detail.label: Bee and Wasp Infestations
themes_detail.summary: Harboring bees/wasps complaints surged to 3 reports 2 WEEKS AGO versus a 0.1 weekly baseline—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—indicating a potential public health or ecological issue warranting pest control and environmental health agency response.
evidence: 3 bee/wasp complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase)
Z-score of 8.69—the second-highest statistical anomaly in the dataset
Timing suggests seasonal or environmental trigger (early spring nesting, new construction attracting hives)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Health Department and Parks to determine if this reflects broader citywide trend or localized environmental change
Interview residents with confirmed hive/wasp nests to understand public health risk and removal response time

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests jumped to 7 complaints LAST WEEK versus a 2.0 weekly average—a 250% spike (z-score: 7.07)—suggesting inadequate sanitation infrastructure in high-foot-traffic areas or accumulating trash from other sources.
evidence: 7 litter basket requests last week vs. 2.0 weekly baseline (250% increase)
Z-score of 7.07 indicates statistically significant spike
Correlates with existing high baseline of litter complaints (500 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Identify specific streets where baskets are missing and cross-check against DPL inventory
Determine if missed collection complaints (688 over 90 days) are contributing to perceived litter shortage

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signs Spike
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints rose to 5 reports 2 WEEKS AGO versus a 1.2 weekly average—a 300% increase (z-score: 8.66)—indicating either vandalism, theft, or deferred maintenance that could create safety and wayfinding hazards.
evidence: 5 missing street sign complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (300% increase)
Z-score of 8.66 ties bee/wasp spike for statistical extremity
Suggests potential pattern of vandalism or accelerated deterioration in public signage
reporting_angles: Walk specific complaint neighborhoods to verify which signs are missing and assess traffic/pedestrian safety impact
Check DOT records for sign replacement requests and maintenance schedules in St. George/Stapleton
